candidates.title: Prefer a trained API retriever over a user-specified API list
candidates.rule: When an agent faces a large API pool, let a trained dense retriever (Sentence-BERT style, contrastively trained on instruction/relevant-API pairs) supply the top-k candidate APIs rather than requiring the user to name the API set; do not assume the human-nominated set is an upper bound.
candidates.passage: using retrieved APIs even improves the performance (both pass rate and win rate) compared to the ground truth API set
candidates.location: Section 3.2, 'Integrating API Retriever with ToolLLaMA' and Table 4
candidates.finding: Feeding ToolLLaMA the top-5 APIs from the trained retriever gave average pass rate 67.3 vs 66.7 with the oracle API set, and win rate 63.1 vs 60.0; the retriever also beat BM25 (17.0) and text-embedding-ada-002 (45.4) at average NDCG@5 with 84.9. The margin over the oracle set is small and within noise on several subsets (e.g. I2-Cat. pass rate fell 77.0 to 68.5), so treat this as 'no worse than oracle', not a reliable gain.
workloads: API retrieval NDCG@1/@5 over 16,464 RapidAPI APIs
candidates.conditions: Retriever trained on ~200k (instruction, relevant API) pairs generated by ChatGPT from the same API hub; top-5 APIs passed into the prompt; pass/win rate judged by ToolEval.
candidates.limitations: In-domain retriever trained on the same API distribution as the test instructions; 'ground truth' APIs were themselves ChatGPT-generated, so the oracle baseline is weak; small and uneven margins; single model and single benchmark; retrieval training cost not quantified.
candidates.validation_test: Hold out instructions whose API labels came from a different source than your retriever's training data, then compare agent success with (a) labeled API set, (b) retriever top-k for k in {3,5,10}, (c) BM25 top-k, reporting per-subset variance across repeated runs.

reason: The paper tests two interventions with matched or cost-controlled comparisons: a DFS-style decision tree over ReACT for multi-step API calling, and feeding retriever-selected APIs instead of the human-specified 'ground truth' API set. Both are concrete harness-level rules. Dataset/benchmark descriptions and ToolEval agreement numbers are not actionable rules on their own.
